status: locked 2026-10-29 after the dev pilot and the change in sensitivity/changes.json (user decision 2026-10-29); test runs use exactly these files
question: Does the result of the locked design depend on protocol entries that copy the benchmark's task wording, or on a library that holds only the ten target protocols?
design_unchanged: The locked source (results/design-lock/lock.json, src/*.py) is not edited. sensitivity/run_sensitivity.py replaces the entries of the institutional libraries in memory and then calls clinical_agent.run.main; sensitivity/libraries.json holds the entries. Their SHA-256 values go into this file at the lock.

conditions.S0: Locked library (existing runs *-test-150-rep1 to -rep3 on GPT-6-Luna, *-test-150-terra* on GPT-6.1-Terra).
conditions.S1_paraphrase: The ten target protocols rewritten in hospital-policy wording with the same facts; terminology and order catalog unchanged.
conditions.S2_realistic: S1, plus about 30 unrelated hospital protocols, about 20 unrelated terminology entries and about 15 unrelated order-catalog entries.
conditions.S3_stress: S2, plus one near-miss protocol per task family (shares words with the topic, governs a different population, indication or setting) and near-miss terminology and catalog entries.
conditions.S4_no_protocols: Locked library without the protocol_search tool (current time, terminology and order catalog stay). Mechanism analysis.

runs.settings: --workers 6 --auth subscription, reasoning effort medium, max steps 17, as the locked runs

hypotheses.H1_primary: Under S2_realistic on GPT-6-Luna, pooled over 3 runs and paired by task, the lower bound of the 95% confidence interval of D - B is above -10 percentage points.
hypotheses.H2: Under S2_realistic on GPT-6-Luna, D(S2) - D(S0) pooled and paired by task has a 95% lower bound above -10 points.
hypotheses.H3: Under S1_paraphrase on GPT-6-Luna, D(S1) - D(S0) has a 95% lower bound above -10 points.
hypotheses.descriptive: S3_stress (D - B and D(S3) - D(S0)) and S4_no_protocols (against C and D(S0)) are reported without a threshold; GPT-6.1-Terra S2 is reported as a second model.
hypotheses.intervals: Paired by task on the per-task mean over runs (normal approximation), and a family-cluster bootstrap (10 000 resamples, seed 1) as a check.
hypotheses.outcomes: passed (primary scorer), passed_upstream and passed_revised as in the main analysis; cost, tool calls and seconds per task.

content_criteria.P1: A paraphrase keeps every criterion, threshold, unit, code, time window, quantity, action, the rule for a missing record and the answer format of the original entry, with the same values.
content_criteria.P2: A paraphrase adds no clinical information and removes none.
content_criteria.P3: A paraphrase shares no run of 6 or more consecutive words with the original entry, counting neither codes nor order text (quoted text and the name of an order-catalog item, such as 'heparin 5000 units SC q8h prophylaxis').
content_criteria.P4: A paraphrase keeps the quoted order text verbatim (for example 'Renal mass follow-up', 'Evaluate renal mass for biopsy or ablation.') and keeps the clinical topic term of the original title in its title.
content_criteria.D1: A distractor is a plausible hospital protocol, terminology entry or catalog entry in the format of the library (topic: criteria and the actions they trigger, with codes).
content_criteria.D2: An unrelated distractor (S2) concerns none of the ten task topics.
content_criteria.D3: A near-miss distractor (S3) shares at least one word with a task topic but states a population, indication or setting that the task goal does not have, so that the goal identifies the target protocol; it does not contradict the target protocol for the target population.
content_criteria.D4: No distractor uses a code of the target entries as a code (445118002, 74177, 90686, 91320, C64.2, CON417, COVIDVACCINE, FT4, HEARTRATE, IMGCT0491, IMGIL0001, NUR1373, QTCINTERVAL, TSH); an analyte name that equals a target code (TSH) may appear with a different code.

dev_pilot.runs: GPT-6-Luna, B and D under S2_realistic and S3_stress, D under S1_paraphrase, once each on dev.
dev_pilot.allowed_changes: Only an entry that violates a content criterion (P1-P4, D1-D4) or a tool that fails to run is changed. A change is decided by reading the entry against the criterion, recorded in sensitivity/changes.json with the criterion and the reason, and is never made because an attempt failed when the entry meets the criteria.
dev_pilot.not_changed: The system prompt, the review, the tools and the locked library.

runs_done.note: Passed of 100 before the change in changes.json.

reporting: Every condition in this plan is reported with its result, whatever the result.
entry_order: Each condition's protocol, terminology and catalog entries are shuffled once with seed 1 (sensitivity/run_sensitivity.py), so target entries do not always come first when search scores tie.
